title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and follow directions, take a rickshaw, bus or train, and give instructions politely or informally.
intro:
Getting around in Maharashtra means rickshaws (रिक्षा), crowded buses, Mumbai's local trains and a lot of asking the way. Directions are given with commands — सरळ जा 'go straight', डावीकडे वळा 'turn left' — so this unit teaches the **imperative** in its informal and polite forms.

You'll also learn the case endings for movement: **-ला** 'to', **-हून / -ऊन** 'from', **-पर्यंत** 'as far as', **-कडे** 'towards' and **-ने** 'by (bus, train)'.

grammar.title: Imperatives: जा, जा; ये, या
grammar.body:
**Informal (तू):** the bare stem: **कर** 'do', **थांब** 'wait', **बस** 'sit', **जा** 'go', **ये** 'come', **घे** 'take', **दे** 'give'.

**Polite (तुम्ही):** stem + **-आ**: **करा**, **थांबा**, **बसा**, **जा**, **या** (ये → या), **घ्या**, **द्या**. This is the standard form for strangers, elders, drivers, shopkeepers.

**Negative:** stem + ऊ + **नकोस** (informal) / **नका** (polite): जाऊ नकोस / जाऊ नका 'don't go'.

**'Let's':** stem + **ऊया** (or ऊ): चल, जाऊया 'come on, let's go'; बसूया 'let's sit'.

Soften with **ना** or **जरा** ('a bit'): जरा थांबा ना 'please wait a moment'.

examples.en: It's late, come on, let's go.

grammar.title: Movement: to, from, as far as, by
grammar.body:
Motion endings attach to the oblique form of the noun:

**-ला** 'to': मुंबईला जाणे 'to go to Mumbai', स्टेशनला 'to the station'
**-त / -मध्ये** 'into': दुकानात जा 'go into the shop'
**-कडे** 'towards; to (a person's place)': डॉक्टरकडे, मामाकडे
**-हून / -ऊन** 'from': पुण्याहून 'from Pune', घरून 'from home'
**-तून** 'out of, through': खिडकीतून 'through the window'
**-पर्यंत** 'as far as, until': स्टेशनपर्यंत
**-ने** 'by (means)': बसने 'by bus', ट्रेनने 'by train'; on foot = **चालत**

The postposition in 'from here / there' is fused: **इथून** 'from here', **तिथून** 'from there', **कुठून** 'from where'.

examples.en: Drop me as far as the station.
Let's go to uncle's place in the evening.

dialogue.title: Finding Shaniwar Wada
dialogue.setting: Jenny, a tourist in Pune, asks a passer-by the way to the historic Shaniwar Wada fort.

lines.speaker: Jenny
lines.en: Excuse me, where is Shaniwar Wada?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.en: Shaniwar Wada? It's quite close from here.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.en: At the second crossroads turn left.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.native: मग पाच मिनिटं चाला. उजवीकडे मोठा दरवाजा दिसेल.
lines.roman: mag pāts miniṭaṃ tsālā. udzvīkaḍe moṭhā darvādzā disel.
lines.en: Then walk five minutes. You'll see a big gate on the right.

lines.speaker: Jenny
lines.en: How long will it take on foot?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.en: Ten or fifteen minutes. Otherwise take a rickshaw.

lines.speaker: Jenny
lines.native: नाही, मी चालत जाते. खूप धन्यवाद!
lines.roman: nāhī, mī tsālat dzāte. khūp dhanyavād!
lines.en: No, I'll walk. Thanks a lot!

culture: To hail a rickshaw you don't say where you want to go and wait for a price — you ask **'…ला येणार का?'** ('will you come to …?'). Drivers may refuse short or out-of-the-way trips. In Mumbai, rickshaws run only in the suburbs; in the south of the city it's black-and-yellow taxis. Landmarks matter more than street names: people will direct you 'past the temple, near the medical shop'.

lessons.title: Asking the way

tip.title: Giving directions: जा, वळा
tip.body:
- To a friend (तू) use the bare stem: **जा**, **ये**, **थांब**, **वळ**.
- To strangers and elders (तुम्ही) add **-आ**: **वळा**, **थांबा**, **बसा**; ये becomes **या**.
- 'Don't': stem + ऊ + **नका** (polite) or **नकोस** (informal): वळू नका 'don't turn'.

new: सरळ जा आणि मग डावीकडे वळा.

sentences.en: Excuse me, which way is the station?
Go straight, then turn right.
Don't turn left here.
The station is up ahead on the right.

sentences.native: तू सरळ ये, मी स्टेशनजवळ आहे.
sentences.roman: tū saraḷ ye, mī sṭeshandzavaḷ āhe.
sentences.en: Come straight here, I'm near the station.
Turn right, then go straight. (informal)
Don't go any further, turn just here.
Is it a long way?

sentences.native: इथून सरळ जा, स्टेशन डावीकडे आहे.
sentences.roman: ithūn saraḷ dzā, sṭeshan ḍāvīkaḍe āhe.
sentences.en: Go straight on from here, the station is on the left.

tip.title: Talking to the driver
tip.body:
- Call the driver **दादा** or **काका** and use the polite forms: **थांबा**, **बसा**, **चला**.
- To ask if he'll take you: place + **-ला येणार का?**
- Soften a request with **जरा** 'a bit' or **ना** at the end: जरा इथे थांबा ना.

sentences.en: Will you go to the station? (to a rickshaw driver)
Please stop here a moment.
Get in the rickshaw.
Stop up ahead, not here.
I'll get off here. (man speaking)
Not a taxi, let's take a rickshaw.
Get off, we're at the station.
Wait a minute, I'm coming. (informal)
Drive slowly, please.

lessons.title: To, from and as far as

tip.title: To, from, as far as, by
tip.body:
- Endings of movement go on the noun: **-ला** 'to', **-हून / -ऊन** 'from', **-पर्यंत** 'as far as', **-कडे** 'to someone's place', **-ने** 'by'.
- Many nouns change first: पुणे → **पुण्याला**, विमानतळ → **विमानतळाला**, घर → **घरून**.
- 'From here' is one word, **इथून**; 'on foot' is **चालत**.

sentences.en: How far is the airport from here?
I need to get to the airport.
Let's walk as far as the station.
What's your address?
Is this address on the map?
I came by rickshaw. (man speaking)
Come over to my place in the evening.
Tomorrow I'm going to the doctor's.

sentences.native: विमानतळ खूप लांब आहे, टॅक्सी घ्या.
sentences.roman: vimāntaḷ khūp lāmb āhe, ṭæksī ghyā.
sentences.en: The airport is very far, take a taxi.
It takes ten minutes from home to the station.

sentences.native: थोडं पुढे चाला, स्टेशन उजवीकडे आहे.
sentences.roman: thoḍaṃ puḍhe tsālā, sṭeshan udzvīkaḍe āhe.
sentences.en: Walk on a little, the station is on the right.

tip.title: Does this bus go to …?
tip.body:
- **बस** and **गाडी** are feminine, so: **ही** बस, **पुढची** गाडी, बस **जाते**.
- 'Does this bus go to Dadar?' = ही बस दादर**ला** जाते **का**?
- For a ticket, name the place with **-चं**: एक तिकीट द्या, पुण्याचं.

sentences.en: Does this bus go to the station?
What time is the next bus?
Two tickets to Mumbai, please.
Does this train stop at Dadar?

sentences.native: हो, पण पुढची गाडी थांबत नाही.
sentences.roman: ho, paṇ puḍhchī gāḍī thāmbat nāhī.
sentences.en: Yes, but the next train doesn't stop.
How much is the bus ticket?
I go to work by bus every day.
I want to get off at the next stop.
Get on quick, the train's leaving!

tip.title: Directions by landmark
tip.body:
- People give directions by landmarks, not street names: **मंदिराजवळ** 'near the temple', **चौकात** 'at the crossroads'.
- The noun changes before जवळ, समोर, -त: मंदिर → **मंदिरा**जवळ, पूल → **पुला**खाली.
- Ordinals take **-या** before an ending: **दुसऱ्या** सिग्नलला, **तिसऱ्या** चौकात.

sentences.en: Turn left at the first traffic light.
The market is near the temple.
Turn left under the flyover.
There's a temple at the third crossroads.
This shop is closed on Sundays.
Come on, let's go to the market.
There's a tea stall in front of the temple.
The light is red, stop!
The shop is past the bridge, on the left.
